items.title: Analyysi: Maailman pysäyttämiseen ei välttämättä tarvita vihollista – digitaalinen korttitalo huojuu omasta painostaan
items.summary: Kun tuhannet matkustajakoneet jämähtävät kiitoteille ja miljoonat työntekijät eri puolilla maailmaa tuijottavat tyhjiä ruutuja, alkaa syyttävä sormi osoitella helposti sinne sun tänne. items.title: SCKit abuses ScreenConnect to deploy remote access and target technician sessions
items.summary: Beginning on November 11, 2026, ConnectWise reported an active campaign of a threat actor gaining unauthorized access to cloud-hosted ConnectWise ScreenConnect instances belonging to managed service providers (MSPs). Microsoft Threat Intelligence has confirmed ConnectWise’s reported activity and we have also observed threat actors abusing ScreenConnect, a legitimate remote-support application, to install unauthorized remote-access clients and deploy a malicious worm, SCKit, on ConnectWise customer managed endpoints. We have identified that the worm targets IT support technician workstations using the hijacked authenticated ScreenConnect Session and uses the victim’s management console to distribute payloads to other managed devices. The resulting access to either target enables threat actors to remotely administer affected endpoints, execute commands, and deploy further tools independently of the legitimate support instance.

items.title: US disrupts North Korean campaign behind $400 million crypto theft
items.summary: The U.S. government has disrupted a North Korean social engineering campaign called ‘FaceStealer’, responsible for stealing more than $400 million in cryptocurrency. The attacks used multiple social engineering techniques, including deepfakes and ClickFix, to target individuals in the cryptocurrency and Web3 sectors, as well as open-source developers. The FaceStealer campaign ran for 18 months before the U.S. seized the underlying cloud-based infrastructure. U.S. authorities identified more than 900 webcam videos that hackers secretly recorded of tech workers, who were deceived in the massive North Korean operation.

items.title: Anthropic Sees AI Agent Swarms Patching Flaws Within a Year
items.summary: "Finding vulnerabilities is the first step," Amodei said. "But if you find 100,000 vulnerabilities, the limitation is patching them, and that is harder to do." The next step, Amodei said, is to turn their agents toward patching assignments. He said Anthropic has already begun working with customers with patching services and noted that Claude models are "getting better at patching more vulnerabilities." The third step is writing more secure code. It is the fourth step that Amodei admits no one is doing quite yet. "The fourth is something that hasn't happened yet. We know that cyberattacks happen in real time and there needs to be a way to solve that in real time. I think in six- to 12-months we'll see swarms of agents that patrol systems and patching these issues at the same time," Amodei said.

items.title: Microsoft Outage Tests Healthcare Cyber Resilience
items.summary: A global Microsoft 365 cloud services outage that disrupted organizations across multiple sectors underscored the need for hospitals and other medical facilities to strengthen operational resilience, manage third-party technology dependencies and prepare for disruptions - even when cyberattacks aren't to blame, experts said.

items.title: FBI flash alert says Artex tool automating cyberattacks at ‘machine speed’
items.summary: Open-source AI platform Artex is being used prolifically by cybercriminals and nation-states to breach government agencies and dozens of critical sectors worldwide, according to a new FBI advisory. The FBI released a flash alert on Friday about the tool, which has caused alarm among cybersecurity experts for its ability to take any large language model and turn it into a powerful hacking tool that can “automate multiple phases of cyber intrusions at machine speed, from reconnaissance through data exfiltration.”

items.title: ACF5000 LCS/CCUS PHP2Shell and OpenSSL Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 9.8, CVEs: CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, CVE-2026-35189, Summary: Three vulnerabilities exist in the PHP and OpenSSL components included in the product versions listed above. An attacker could exploit the two PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) by sending specially crafted web requests to the web server of the system node, causing remote code execution. An attacker could exploit the OpenSSL vulnerability (CVE-2026-35189) by sending a specially crafted certificate to the mutual TLS server (TCP port 9001) of the system node, causing a denial of service.

items.title: ‘We need more reviewers’: Finding Linux bugs is easy now – fixing them is another story
items.summary: It’s not all doom and gloom, though. Linux Torvalds, Linux’s creator, said in a recent Linux Kernel Mailing List (LKML) message that much of the new code in the Linux 7.4 rc 2 “was driven by various AI fixes.” He continued, “that on the bpf [Berkeley Packet Filter]- side at least the fixes are now coming in faster than the new reports, and that sounds lovely if true. I think most other areas haven’t reached that point yet, but it’s at least a sign that we _may_ be starting to see the tide starting to turn. Don’t hold your breath, but maybe cross your fingers we’ll be getting there in the not entirely distant future.” We can but hope. In an interview, Kroah-Hartman isn’t so optimistic. “We are getting closer, yes, but not quite there yet.” He’s not even willing to give a guesstimate of when human-approved AI fixes will catch up with and overcome AI bug reports.

items.title: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop that disrupted thousands of flights, White House says no indication of "nefarious act"
items.summary: "What we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system," [Transportation Secretary Sean] Duffy said during the news conference. " ... Our routers actually got overloaded with data and … they started to give us inconsistency in the data from those routers. And because of that, we shut the system down." An update to the private communications network that connects America's air traffic control system caused the system to reboot, leading to a crash and a communications outage, multiple sources told CBS News earlier Friday. The system is operated by L3Harris, which did not immediately respond to CBS News' request for comment.
